newsitem.title: UK: Mideast VLCCs stay firm on lack of modern ships.
newsitem.headline: Mideast VLCCs stay firm on lack of modern ships.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) ended the week on a firm note, with an acute shortage of modern vessels in recent weeks pushing the market up the few remaining ships, brokers said.
VLCCs on Mideast/east voyages rose towards the W65 level, while rates on the relatively few fixtures to the U.S. Gulf achieved W52.5.

Brokers Galbraith's Ltd said in their weekly tanker report that "this is a slightly earlier upwards surge than last year and from a low point of about W47-1/2 compared with the 1996 low point of about W42-1/2."
But they noted that this year bunker prices are slightly higher by about $6 for 380 cst at Fujairah.
Galbraith's figures show that this year's Mideast/Japan average of W62.17 is well above the level of W44.45 for this week in 1996.
Brokers said trans-Atlantic VLCC trade was thin, but the 290,000 tonne Golar Glasgow was on Friday reported fixed Norway/U.S. Gulf at W60 for Statoil.
Galbraith's said that because of the light fixing there were signs that owners in the Atlantic Basin have been content to accept a fall of a couple of points for cargoes on their dates.
But they added: "Any increase in enquiry next week will see this turn around very quickly, as tonnage is not shown as being over-abundant."
While there were few West Africa VLCC fixtures, the Suezmax (130,000 tonne) sector was active with rates steady at about W95.
In the Mediterranean and Black Sea Suezmaxes were fixed at W95/97.5 but the 80,000 tonne (Aframax) market remained quiet at W102.5.
Brokers said North Sea Aframax trade was active but a surfeit of ships kept rates down to around W90.
Fuel oil firmed in Europe, with 25,000 inter-UKC at W185 and cross-Med at W195.

The Caribbean market remained slower than recent weeks, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W170 on Friday, down from a year high of W245 but well above the year low of W115. Fuel oil cargoes were steady at W215.
